newsitem.title: USA: U.S. jobless claims rose in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jobless claims rose in latest week.

text.p: U.S. Labor Department report of initial state jobless benefit claims, seasonally adjusted.
Week Ended Initial Claims 4-Week Avg. Continued Claims
R-Revised, April 19 Initial Claims from 324,000; April 19 4-week average from 323,000; April 12 Continued Claims from 2,290,000 and April 5 from 2,294,000.
Wall Street economists had forecast initial jobless claims of 325,000 in the April 26 week.
Labor said two states reported increases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended April 19, the latest period for which data are available.
Missouri reported 2,263 additional claims because of layoffs in the transportation industry. Rhode Island, with 1,053, had no comment on the increase.
Fourteen states and one territory reported decreases in claims exceeding 1,000 in the April 19 week.
The largest included North Carolina, with 5,239 fewer claims; Texas, with 4,103; Pennsylvania, with 4,033; New York, with 3,250; Tennessee, with 3,102; Alabama, 2,981; and Wisconsin, with 2,318.

North Carolina cited fewer layoffs in the textile, furniture and transportation equipment industries. Pennyslvania had fewer layoffs in the trade, food and stone/clay/glass industries. Tennessee cited fewer layoffs in the food, textile, apparel, rubber/plastics, industrial machinery, trade and service industries.

Alabama reported fewer layoffs in the trade and service industries and manufacturing. Wisconsin had fewer layoffs in the construction, trade and service industries and manufacturing. New York and Texas had no comment.

The Labor Department said the last time initial claims had reached this level was for the January 4 week when first-time applications totaled 365,000. The seasonally adjusted four-week moving average was at its highest since the January 25 week, when claims were reported at 339,750.
